families.whatWasMeasured: All fifteen obligations. Both fixtures and all four committed raster PNGs rehashed and matched their recorded hashes and byte lengths, and the two fixture hashes match the hash-bound RASTER_PASS receipt from workflow run 33574304514. The zero-source binding was checked against the MASTER_QUEUE row (boundCount 0, officialFormFamily NONE, forms []) and both grounding records were confirmed to exist and to carry the cited track and packetSetId. Every printed SPBI fee figure ($36, $75, $75, $15), the payee 'Treasurer-State of CT' and the DESPP-SPBI mailing address were verified character-for-character against the held DPS-0846-C bytes in the mounted corpus.
families.theDefect: The delivered guidance carries a paragraph headed 'ONE RUMOUR TO IGNORE' telling the participant that the requirement for the SPBI report to be 'dated on or after January 1, 2024' looks like a misreading and that 'nothing found requires the report to bear a post-2024 date'. The mounted corpus holds DESPP-0847-C, the DESPP form for a clean-slate erasure hearing, whose printed instruction 2 states the opposite as mandatory: the criminal history record 'must be dated on or after 01/01/2024', and without it 'your submission will be deemed incomplete and your request for a review and/or hearing will be denied'. The packet therefore instructs the participant to disregard a documented requirement whose breach the source says causes denial.
families.whyThisIsAFailAndNotABlock: The finding does not depend on mapping the gated form to this track — which the corpus forbids while Connecticut's state legal review is missing. It needs only that the packet asserted an unqualified negative about what the record contains, and that assertion is false against the repository at this base. That is a packet-content defect and a repair, not an open legal input.
families.repair: Replace the instruction to disregard the ≥01/01/2024 record date with a statement that a DESPP form held in the Master Library imposes it, that the currentness gate on that asset is open, and that the participant should obtain a current report and confirm with DESPP. Do not bind, render or fill DESPP-0847-C.
families.notFailed: FILING_DESTINATION was deliberately NOT failed. The stage-1 destination is stated in full and verified against held bytes. The gated DESPP-0847-C also carries a stage-2 destination, but stating it would require mapping a source-gated asset to this track, which CT's STATE_README forbids while the state legal review is missing. Amendment A1 does not compel a packet to publish a destination drawn from an asset the corpus itself says must not yet be mapped.

families.whatWasMeasured: All fifteen obligations, none unmeasured. Both fixtures rehashed and matched the RASTER_PASS receipt bindings from run 33574304514. All six writes read back off the delivered bytes directly. The boundary fixture was inspected for clipping, where a 99-character address wraps cleanly and a 60-character email prints complete. The authority for composing a custom petition rather than filling a form was traced to two held sources: the corpus MA legal review Track 8, which records the existence of a BMC form as unresolved, and the corpus governance file ADOPTED_BATCH_2_LEGAL_RESEARCH_RESOLUTION.md line 129, which authorises a counsel-approved custom consolidated petition where no current BMC form is published. Fee, service and filing destination were each tested against MA.memo.json and the corpus Track 8 before scoring.
nonBlockingObservations: The packet says the consolidated petition 'SUPPLEMENTS the statewide per-case form' without naming that form TC0057, which the held review and the Batch 2 resolution both name. Scored a PASS because TC0057 is correctly not a component of this packet and the clerk of the venue division is named as the authority, but naming it would be an improvement.

The held review records that the final hearing is set 30 to 45 days out and that § 100C ¶2 requires the Clerk-Magistrate to post the petition on a public bulletin board until the hearing. The packet conveys 'public notice' without those two specifics.
families.reviewStillOutstanding: The Batch 2 resolution authorises a COUNSEL-APPROVED custom consolidated petition. Counsel approval is not this lane's to give and is not implied by this PASS.

families.whatWasMeasured: All fifteen obligations, none unmeasured. Both fixtures rehashed and matched the RASTER_PASS receipt bindings from run 33574304514, which covers all 8 pages. families.whyItPasses: This family answers the fee question on the strongest branch of the standard — it states that the application is free, sourced to NRS 179A.160 — and correctly separates the record-copy fee as a different service. It states that the section prescribes no delivery method rather than inventing one, and it declines to offer the NRS 179.245(9) sex-trafficking waiver because that waiver is confined by its own words to petitions under NRS 179.245 and does not reach this section. The refusals to over-claim are as load-bearing as the assertions.

families.theDefect: The case number the court assigns at filing is classified two contradictory ways in one packet. On the petition, primary_filing.case_number is refused as court_prosecutor_clerk_or_agency_owned because 'the court assigns it at filing'. On the proposed order, proposed_order.order_case_number carries completenessClass null and is listed among the seven requiredBeforeFiling items with the instruction to supply 'the case number, if the court assigned one at filing' — a value that by its own stated reason cannot exist before filing, on a document filed together with the petition. The contradiction reaches the participant: participant-instructions.md line 42 lists it under 'The items you must supply' while line 58 of the same file lists the petition's identical case number under 'Things the platform deliberately left blank'.
families.severity: This is the same defect class the lane already failed on ny_mrta_marijuana-set — a court-owned field surfaced as a participant obligation, with the file contradicting itself — but a materially milder instance: one field rather than three, a hedged label, no mojibake, and no court-use-only block violated. It is failed for consistency with that precedent and because the repair is small and exact, and the severity difference is recorded so a Captain can right-size it.
families.repair: Reclassify proposed_order.order_case_number to match primary_filing.case_number so it leaves the requiredBeforeFiling set and moves from the 'items you must supply' table to the 'deliberately left blank' list. The blank itself stays on the delivered page; only its classification and disclosure are wrong.
families.judgementCallRecorded: SERVICE was scored PASS after establishing that no bound record imposes a service or notice duty for § 99-15-59. The DA-notice material in the bound compiled profile's clause list is attributed on its face to § 99-19-71(2)(b) and to §§ 9-11-15(3) and 21-23-7(6) — different provisions — and the build correctly declined to import it. MS.memo.json has no track for § 99-15-59 at all and the corpus MS legal review never mentions the section. Flagged rather than failed: the memo's ms-nonconv track records that some Mississippi districts expect prosecutor notice as local practice, and this packet carries no such caution — but that record is for § 99-19-71(4), and importing it across statutes is the cross-route inference this factory forbids.

forTheCaptain.issue: Connecticut's recorded true output blocker may not be a blocker at all.
forTheCaptain.detail: ct-missed-erasure-set records DESPP's 'form and manner' for a § 54-142t(g) submission as a true output blocker that 'had not been located'. The mounted Master Library holds DESPP-0847-C — sha256 08658dc45d7d41c20a26dcab54fff8756302e85bef7f4d519d9c0a3d4e4fbcfc — an 18-field acroform whose corpus origin filename records it as new at 2024-01-01, the date the § 54-142t(g) remedy became available. Its face requires the criminal history record 'demonstrating that such conviction has not been marked as erased', which is verbatim the statutory proof this track describes. It also carries the stage-2 filing destination (DESPP, Attn: Legal Affairs Unit, 1111 Country Club Road, Middletown, CT 06457), an online submission option, and the SPBI phone (860) 685-8480 option 4.
forTheCaptain.whyItIsStuck: The asset sits in 05_SOURCE_GATED with freshness_status source_or_currentness_gate_open and generation_allowed no, and Connecticut's STATE_README records the state legal review as missing and forbids mapping form assets to eligibility tracks until it is supplied. So this lane could neither bind it nor treat it as established.
forTheCaptain.decisionNeeded: Whether to commission Connecticut's missing state legal review and open a source-promotion question on DESPP-0847-C. If it is the instrument, stage 2 of this family is buildable and the recorded blocker is stale.
